- The first evaluation invocation wrote predictions and summary metrics, then failed while reading the empty collection-retry CSV during report assembly. Empty diagnostics are now handled explicitly, and the evaluation/report rerun completed successfully.

PHASE 1 DATA CONSISTENCY (fixed scope: 2024-01-02..2026-11-04)
Raw per-date cache row counts: SPX 1,322,358; SPXW 8,500,017 (714 cached dates per root). Merged option_chains_spx.csv counts: SPX 1,194,080; SPXW 6,803,711. The discrepancy is filtering, not missing roots: the chain retains DTE 7..60 and valid nonnegative, non-crossed bid/ask quotes. For SPX, all 1,194,080 rows in the DTE range pass quote validation. For SPXW, 6,803,712 rows are in range and one additional row is removed by quote validation, leaving 6,803,711. Thus the raw-to-chain reductions are 128,278 SPX rows and 1,696,306 SPXW rows.
The full repository pytest suite passed: 9 tests.
Proposed-only 30D-smile fallback: search outward to the nearest expiry on each side with at least 5 unique finite total-variance points, retain the existing 20-point common-moneyness-coverage requirement, then interpolate using those two expiries. This would rescue 1 of the 7 failed dates (2024-12-02; valid upper fallback 2025-01-31 with 60 DTE). The other six dates do not have a qualifying pair with sufficient shared moneyness coverage. This fallback was not applied.

The raw ThetaData response includes a `created` timestamp, preserved through the chain and IV files. The separate `timestamp` alias is empty; the previous missing-timestamp count checked that empty alias rather than `created`. `created` is a common EOD snapshot time, not an update time per contract, so quote staleness cannot be inferred from it. Last-trade time is not quote freshness.

GAUSSIAN-SHAPE MOMENT BASELINE SANITY
No leakage or arithmetic bug was found. Standardizing moment features reduced the training design condition number from 5.325e3 to 4.508 but produced the same forecasts to numerical precision; no test forecast variance was clipped. Predicted test variance averaged 1.022 times realized variance (correlation 0.745). The baseline assumes a Gaussian quantile shape and carries the input mean forward. Test target absolute skewness had median 0.791. A Gaussian using the target's true mean and variance still had mean W2 8.031003e-03 versus 8.330430e-03 for this baseline, while persistence was 2.719857e-03. The poor result is consistent with Gaussian shape misspecification for skewed RNDs, not feature scaling or leakage; no baseline code change was made.

PHASE 2 MARTINGALE-MISS CURVE DIAGNOSTICS (diagnostic only; no pipeline change)
For each date, the pre/post means below are moments of the second-difference density from the interpolated Black-76 call curve before and after the existing call-price projection, with each in-grid density normalized to unit mass. The pre-projection density is clipped at zero using the production rule; clipping changed the reported means by less than 0.01 points. The post-projection mean matches the saved extracted mean to displayed precision.

Finding: the miss is already present before call-price projection. Projection shifts the mean by only 0..9.12 index points (max absolute shift 9.12), versus final misses of 52.66..150.07 points. The finite strike grid is the leading identified cause: raw in-grid mass is 0.902..0.964, so about 3.6%..9.8% of probability mass is omitted; discrete endpoint call slopes assign about 3.6%..9.2% below the lower strike and at most 0.356% above the upper strike. The existing code then normalizes the truncated in-grid density, whose lower-tail omission raises its conditional mean. The reported q01/q99 values are percentiles of that normalized in-grid density, not full-tail percentiles; the left-tail estimate exceeding 1% on every date means the true q01 is outside the grid.
SVI wing extrapolation is not the cause in the current path: fit_iv_curve.py evaluates the fitted SVI only between the observed smile's minimum and maximum k, and Breeden-Litzenberger consumes that bounded curve. The density grid endpoints are exactly the observed fitted-curve strike endpoints.
Proposed fix, not applied: extend the strike grid with explicitly documented SVI/Black-76 wing treatment, check convergence of omitted tail mass and first moment as the range expands, and impose/validate total mass 1 and first moment equal to the forward before scoring. Avoid treating simple renormalization of the truncated interior density as a full-support RND. Validate the proposed tail completion against the current extraction on these nine dates and ordinary dates before changing production behavior.

PHASE 3 WASSERSTEIN GP FRAGILITY (descriptive evaluation; no model changes)
Primary split: target-date cutoff 2026-04-14, 143 test pairs per horizon. Leave-one-out and joint miss-date exclusions remove training pairs with either endpoint on an excluded date; primary test pairs are unchanged. April exclusion removes training pairs touching any of 21 April 2025 RND dates.
Rolling-origin uses expanding training at 50%, 65%, and 80% calendar cutoffs with non-overlapping test blocks; every post-50% target is scored once and hyperparameters are refit at each origin.
Skill = 1 - model mean loss / persistence mean loss. NW CIs use h-1 lags; sensitivity uses 5 lags at h=1 and 10 at h=5. Moving-block bootstrap uses 5,000 resamples, fixed seed 20261106, block h and block 10. Holm-adjusted p-values use one family across all scenario, horizon, and loss comparisons.
Detailed local/ignored rows are in wasserstein_gp_fragility.csv. Gamma/noise/optimizer/Cholesky, fallback and concentration diagnostics are included; the implementation has no separate numerical jitter parameter.

PHASE 4 QUANTILE-CHANGE MODEL COMPARISON
Primary evaluation is rolling-origin with expanding training at the 50%, 65%, and 80% calendar cutoffs and non-overlapping test blocks. The fixed 80/20 split at 2026-04-14 is secondary. Both use exact calendar h=1/h=5 pairs and common pair indices across models.
All RNDs are represented by nondecreasing nonnegative quantiles on the fixed 200-point probability grid, rescaled to arithmetic mean one. Models predict target-minus-input quantile changes. Every forecast, including persistence, uses the same isotonic, nonnegative, mean-one projection before W2 scoring. The zero-change projection reproduces persistence exactly.
CV uses three expanding forward-chaining folds (training prefixes 50%, 65%, and 80% of each outer training window). Selection minimizes pooled inner validation squared W2 after projection. Every GP uses gamma multipliers {0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10} of the training median heuristic and standardized-output noise/regularization ratios {1e-6, 1e-4, 1e-2, 1e-1, 1}. Ridge autoregression uses the same regularization grid. Test performance uses CV-selected values only; the full parameter sweep for each outer split is separately labelled sensitivity-only. Training-condition sensitivity is reported both with all eligible training pairs and after dropping every training pair with either endpoint in April 2025.
Models: PCA-factor quantile-change GP (main), PCA-factor linear autoregression, GP on volatility/skewness/kurtosis, GP on SVI parameters, Wasserstein-input GP predicting quantile changes (continuity of Wasserstein input geometry), persistence, and legacy Wasserstein autoregression. This phase's Wasserstein GP row is change-output/CV-tuned and is not the previous variance-regression plus barycenter implementation.
SVI feature diagnostic: 5 optimizer status failures among 707 SVI rows; 5 have finite parameter vectors and were retained as SVI-GP inputs to keep the common date/pair set. Dates: 2024-04-12,2025-02-26,2025-03-27,2025-05-12,2026-09-08.
Bootstrap resamples=5000, seed=20261106; block lengths h and 10. NW primary lags h-1; sensitivity 5 at h=1 and 10 at h=5. Holm adjustment is performed across model, horizon, and loss comparisons separately within each evaluation, training-condition, and regime group.
Execution note: the first report-formatting pass raised a KeyError when it requested paired inference for the persistence reference, which intentionally has no model-vs-persistence differential. The saved forecast and inference tables were intact; the formatter was corrected to report persistence as the zero-skill reference, and this report was regenerated from those tables.
